atproto.handle_shim: mirror.gcr.io/library/nginx:alpine publishing 127.0.0.1:80 -> the PDS with Host preserved (a handle carries no port, so handle->DID resolution can only hit 80/443)
atproto.handles: alice/bob/carol/dave .localtest.me — a public domain that answers 127.0.0.1

lab.no_public_network: every issuer, JWKS, token endpoint, PDS and redirect URI is a 127.0.0.1 or localhost address. What reached the network: the npm install of the PDS, the nginx pull, DNS for *.localtest.me, and one accidental AWS reachability attempt from a container boot that still had the env template's placeholder S3 credentials (replaced with STORAGE_BACKEND=local immediately).

defect_found.symptom: the whole round trip completes, step_up_tokens holds the row UNSPENT, and POST /auth/me/password/set answers 403 step_up_required — every run
defect_found.mechanism: a step-up completes as a TOP-LEVEL redirect; that navigation discards the SPA's in-memory access token, so the landing page redeems a new one from the refresh cookie, and Refresh rotates (revokes the session row, creates a new one). The token is bound to (user, session), so the binding is destroyed by the very page load that receives it.
defect_found.measured: the step-up grant at 14:04:49.727 bound session b10959f9…; that session was revoked at 14:04:49.826 and replaced; the set at 14:04:52.908 came from 48160b27… -> 403, audit auth.password.set failure step_up_required
defect_found.why_the_tests_missed_it: TestStepUpSetPasswordEndToEnd holds one bearer from sign-in and never refreshes in the middle, which no browser can do
defect_found.fix: vidra-core #225 — carry a LIVE assertion onto the session that replaces the one it was bound to (one new query on the 0144 table; no migration, no OpenAPI change)

env_file.render_without_the_file: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file <filled> config -q — clean
env_file.render_with_the_file: clean, and with --profile core --profile worker --profile frontend the rendered api AND worker environments each carry OAUTH_PROVIDERS + OAUTH_DEX_ISSUER/_CLIENT_ID/_CLIENT_SECRET/_SCOPES — five keys where A05 measured one
env_file.lab_note: the worker sits behind the `worker` profile, not `core`: a render with only --profile core --profile frontend contains no worker service at all, and reading 'the worker has no OAUTH keys' out of it would be wrong
env_file.container_boot_with_the_file: ghcr.io/yegamble/vidra-core:v0.6.2 through `docker compose … run --rm --no-deps api`: 'oauth provider configured provider=dex issuer=https://sso.example.org/dex', then 'http server starting', and GET /api/v1/instance answers oauth_providers: ["dex"]
env_file.container_boot_without_the_file: the same command, same env file, file moved aside: fatal 'config: OAUTH_DEX_ISSUER must be a valid http(s) URL / OAUTH_DEX_CLIENT_ID is required / OAUTH_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET is required' — exactly the A05 failure
env_file.gitignore: vidra-core/.gitignore:78 env/*.env — `git check-ignore -v env/oauth.env` confirms the filled file cannot be committed

not_proven: any hosted IdP (Google/Okta/Entra quirks: audience arrays, email_verified as a string, id_token algorithms other than RS256)
an https PUBLIC_BASE_URL, so neither a production redirect-URI registration nor the ATProto hosted client-metadata client was exercised (unchanged from A05/A30)
provider-initiated or back-channel logout — vidra implements none
delivery failure to the .invalid placeholder: Mailpit accepts every recipient, so the 'this address can never receive mail' claim is architectural here, not measured
the container boot used the v0.6.2 release image (the newest one on this machine), so it proves env_file DELIVERY and the boot gate, not this branch's code in a container
